title: Partner Co-sell Pipeline Review - Apex Partners
summary: Quarterly co-sell pipeline sync to surface high-priority joint opportunities, align on joint motion for two enterprise deals, and confirm technical readiness for Dedicated/private options. Action items: Redwood to send updated co-sell deck and playbook; Apex to nominate two target accounts for joint outreach; schedule dedicated demo and benchmark lane for top deal.
next_steps: Redwood to share updated co-sell playbook and tailored deck by 2026-03-06
Apex to provide list of top 2 target accounts for joint outreach by 2026-03-09
Schedule Redwood Dedicated demo + perf baseline for Deal A week of 2026-03-09

Lena Ortiz - provide top 2 target accounts and intro emails - 2026-03-09

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Apex Channel Lead), Tom Becker (Apex Sales Ops), Priya Nair (Apex Tech Dir)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for carving out time we wanted to run through the co-sell pipeline and make sure we're aligned on next steps for the two big deals you surfaced last week. Diego and I will cover the technical bits and I'll call out GTM actions.
[00:28] Lena Ortiz: awesome, thanks Maya. quick note we only have 50 minutes, so if we could focus on Deal A and Deal B that's ideal.
[00:41] Tom Becker: yea and also any notes on "badge" or partner sell motion, our reps keep asking who is the primary owner.
[00:55] Diego Ramos: ok quick tech preface — for Deal A we recommend starting with Redwood Dedicated; the workload needs consistent throughput and the customer has strict data isolation requirements. dedicated gives predictable latency and simpler audit trails.
[01:17] Priya Nair: when you say Dedicated, do you mean Redwood Dedicated pool in the cloud or the private deployment? customer is asking about VPC and KMS.
[01:29] Diego Ramos: good q. Dedicated (reserved capacity) lives in Redwood's managed infra but we can configure VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for keys. if they need on-prem or air-gapped then Redwood Private is the option but that's a longer path.
[01:48] Lena Ortiz: margin question — how much of a lift vs hosted? our rev org will push for hosted if cost difference is large.
[01:56] Maya Chen: typical tradeoff: hosted is fastest and lowest friction, Dedicated gives better unit economics at scale and isolation. for Deal A the buyer has latency SLOs and compliance asks so Dedicated seems the right balance. we can show cost delta in the deck.
[02:16] Tom Becker: are there any blockers around SOC2 or enterprise audit docs?
[02:23] Maya Chen: nope we have SOC2, ISO attestations and can provide audit logs; Diego can share the security pack after.
[02:31] Diego Ramos: yeah i'll drop the security + architecture slide deck, includes KMS, RBAC, and audit log flow. note: some of the terms in our posh docs are abbreviated, sometimes the transcript shows KV cache as K-V cash ha, so just fyi.
[02:51] Lena Ortiz: sweet. moving to pipeline specifics, Deal A is a finance platform (named Acuity Financial) — current state: proof-of-concept with internal pilot, budgeting for Q3, champion is VP of Eng. Deal B is a marketing automation platform (named BrightWave) — POC planned, procurement timeline unclear.
[03:18] Maya Chen: great, for Acuity Financial what is the technical evaluation scope? are they testing latency, throughput, or hallucination rates?
[03:28] Priya Nair: they care about latency for live agent augmentation and cost per inference for 24/7 usage. also redaction and data retention policies.
[03:36] Diego Ramos: ok so two bench metrics: p50/p95 latency at expected QPS and cost model. we should run a Dedicated perf lane simulating their prompt mix.
[03:48] Tom Becker: can Redwood do a short benchmark we can share with the sponsor?
[03:53] Maya Chen: yes, Diego can run a perf baseline; we usually do a 2-week sandbox for realistic prompts.
[04:00] Diego Ramos: caveat: sandbox perf is representative but real production mixed loads and KV cache patterns can shift numbers. we recommend enabling prefix caching and tuning batching parameters; that usually saves tokens and improves p95 under burst.
[04:20] Lena Ortiz: ok on pricing how does co-sell credit or partner rebate work?
[04:25] Maya Chen: we have partner discounts for co-sell deals and can include a margin for your channel partners, details in the partner playbook i'll share. usually structured as a percentage rebate on committed Dedicated spend.
[04:40] Tom Becker: competitors? sales keep asking between Redwood vs Bedrock vs Anthropic.
[04:46] Maya Chen: Bedrock is more infra focused and customers sometimes pick it for deep AWS integrations; Anthropic is strong on safety; Redwood's differentiation is production-focused inference + unified ops across hosted/dedicated/private which simplifies rollouts.
[05:02] Priya Nair: any known limits for model variants? like if Acuity wants a quantized custom model?
[05:09] Diego Ramos: we support quantization profiles and we can onboard model variants. custom models are possible but onboarding timelines vary; we should scope that if Acuity wants to bring their own model.
[05:22] Lena Ortiz: good. next up, joint GTM — what assets will you give us?
[05:27] Maya Chen: playbook, co-sell deck, partner badge, joint one-pager, and a sell sheet for Deal A tailored to finance use-cases. we'll also provide battlecards covering common objections: cost vs latency, dedicated vs hosted, security.
[05:44] Tom Becker: can we get a concise 2-slide tech summary that the reps can hand off to customers?
[05:50] Diego Ramos: yes i'll make a 2-slide perf + security summary.
[06:00] [10:14] -- (segment jump) Maya Chen: re: Deal B, BrightWave, they are more sensitive to costs and may accept hosted to start. plan: start hosted POC with guardrails, then migrate to Dedicated if throughput and SLA justify it.
[06:28] Lena Ortiz: BrightWave wants an integration with their existing CRM and wants to keep vectors local — is that supported?
[06:35] Diego Ramos: we can support hybrid approaches: keep embeddings in their VPC and use Redwood for inference with securely managed peering. some of the language in the legal docs is fiddly but we can get legal synced.
[06:50] Tom Becker: will Redwood sign customer-level DPA and security addenda?
[06:55] Maya Chen: yes — Redwood has standard DPAs and we can do enterprise addenda for jurisdictional requirements. legal typically takes a few rounds.
[07:05] Priya Nair: i noticed in previous notes there was mention of "auto-fallback to smaller model variants" when capacity constrained — does that happen in Dedicated?
[07:15] Diego Ramos: fallback policies exist at routing layer; for Dedicated we can pin to a model version but also configure fallback rules to a compatible variant to avoid outage. we can surface those rules in the runbook.
[07:30] Lena Ortiz: what about tracking co-sell credit in CRM? any automation?
[07:36] Maya Chen: we can add Redwood as a partner in your CRM and include a CRM deal tag we populate; we also provide a referral code to track leads. we'll send the CRM integration notes.
[07:48] Tom Becker: great — about the demo, can we get a focused one that shows Dedicated deployment with KMS and audit logs?
[07:56] Diego Ramos: yes, Diego to run dedicated demo. Diego: action item to prepare demo config and perf checklist.
[08:05] Maya Chen: recapping next steps quickly — Maya to send playbook and deck by Friday; Lena to nominate 2 accounts; Diego to prepare demo; schedule the demo for week of 3/9. any other asks?
[08:18] Lena Ortiz: can you include a one-page cost comparison table? our finance folks will need that.
[08:24] Maya Chen: will do.
[08:30] Tom Becker: ok thanks all, we'll follow up via the thread and expect materials.
[08:36] [51:59] Meeting end: quick informal chat about conference plans, off record small talk.

Notes on transcript quality: medium — occasional mis-attribution, small transcription artifacts (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cash"), some sentence fragments.

References/attachments mentioned: co-sell playbook (link to be shared), Dedicated demo config (internal doc), security pack (link), partner badge assets (link).

Explicit next steps (verbatim):
- Redwood: send co-sell deck, playbook, partner badge assets by 2026-03-06.
- Apex: provide top 2 target accounts and intro emails by 2026-03-09.
- Redwood SE: prepare Dedicated demo config and perf checklist by 2026-03-10.

End of transcript.
